title: Chicken Karahi

description: Chicken Karahi is a quintessential Pakistani dish, renowned for its rich, spicy tomato-based gravy and tender chicken cooked in a traditional karahi wok. This flavorful curry is a staple in Pakistani homes and restaurants, celebrated for its robust taste from fresh ginger, garlic, and green chilies. It is best enjoyed hot with fresh naan, roti, or rice, making it a perfect hearty meal for any occasion.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat oil or ghee in a large karahi or wok over high heat. Add the chicken pieces and fry until they turn light golden brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. This helps to seal in the juices.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics and Spices
instructions.text: Reduce heat to medium. Add the ginger-garlic paste to the karahi and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Stir in cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Cook for another 2 minutes, ensuring the spices are well coated.

instructions.title: Cook the Tomatoes
instructions.text: Add the chopped or pureed tomatoes to the chicken. Increase heat to medium-high and cook, stirring frequently, until the tomatoes soften and the oil separates from the masala, approximately 8-10 minutes. Mash the tomatoes lightly with the back of your spoon.

instructions.title: Simmer and Tenderize
instructions.text: Pour in 1/2 cup of water, cover the karahi, and reduce the heat to low. Let it simmer for 10-12 minutes, or until the chicken is tender and cooked through. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Finish with Yogurt and Chilies
instructions.text: If using, stir in the plain yogurt and continue to cook on medium heat for 2-3 minutes until the yogurt is fully incorporated and the gravy thickens slightly. Add the slit green chilies and freshly ground black pepper.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Sprinkle with garam masala powder, julienned fresh ginger, and fresh chopped coriander. Give it a gentle stir. Serve the authentic Pakistani Chicken Karahi hot with naan, roti, or rice.

tips: Always use fresh, good quality tomatoes; they are key to the Karahi's distinctive flavor and texture. For a smoother gravy, you can blanch and peel them before chopping.
Adjust the spice levels to your preference. For an extra kick, add more green chilies or a pinch of red chili flakes at the end.
Authentic Karahi is traditionally cooked in a wok-like pan, allowing for even heat distribution and quick cooking. Serve immediately with hot naan or roti for the best experience.
